title: Ethiopian Chemistry University Entrance Exam 2014
description: Ethiopian Chemistry University Entrance Exam 2014 featuring 80 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: What is the significance of electron probability distribution? It tells us about
options: the probability of finding an electron is very far away from the nucleus.
finding the electron very close to the nucleus at all times.
finding the electron in its orbit at a particular time.
the space containing its most likely path for electrons.
questions.explanation:
In quantum mechanics, electrons do not move in fixed circular orbits like planets.

 Instead, the electron probability distribution describes the region of space around the nucleus where the probability of finding an electron is highest.

 This region is called an orbital.

 It does not give the exact position or time of the electron, but rather the most likely space where the electron can be found.

questions.questionText: Which group in the periodic table contains elements with the valence electron configuration of ns²np¹?
options: IV
III
II
I
questions.explanation:
Elements with the valence electron configuration ns²np¹ have three electrons in their outermost shell.

 Such elements belong to Group III (also called Group 13) of the periodic table, which includes elements like boron, aluminium, gallium, indium, and thallium.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a correct Lewis structure for diazomethane?
options: A.
B.
C.
D.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a property of covalent compounds? Covalent compounds
options: is crystalline solids at room temperature.
is generally insoluble in water.
has high melting and boiling points.
is non-volatile.
questions.explanation:
Covalent compounds are formed by sharing of electrons and usually exist as discrete molecules.

 They generally have low melting and boiling points, are often volatile, and are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.

 Therefore, the correct property is that they are generally insoluble in water.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a covalent molecule?
options: CO₃²
[NH₄]⁺
NaCl
PCl₅
questions.explanation:
PCl₅ (phosphorus pentachloride) is a covalent molecule because it is formed by sharing of electrons between non-metal atoms (phosphorus and chlorine).

 CO₃²⁻ and NH₄⁺ are polyatomic ions, while NaCl is an ionic compound.

questions.questionText: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory was modified by the modern atomic theory?
options: Compounds are formed when atoms of more than one element combine.
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions.
Atoms are indivisible and indestructible.
Atoms are the smallest particles of all elements.
questions.explanation:
Dalton's postulate that atoms are indivisible and indestructible was disproven and modified. 

Modern atomic theory established that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) and can be destroyed or changed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following includes all of the known atomic models?
options: Bohr Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model, Dalton's Atomic Model, de Broglie Model
Bohr Model, the Quantum Mechanical Model, Rutherford Model, Thomson Model, Dalton's Atomic Model
Bohr Model, the Quantum Mechanical Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model
Bohr Model, Quantum Mechanical Model, Dalton's Atomic Model, Valence Bond Model
questions.explanation:
The major historical atomic models are Dalton's atomic model, Thomson's model, Rutherford's nuclear model, Bohr's atomic model, and the Quantum Mechanical model.

 The other options either omit Dalton's model or include models (such as de Broglie or Valence Bond) that are not complete atomic models.

questions.questionText: The electron configuration of Cu (Z=29) is:
options: [Ar]4s¹3d¹⁰
[Kr]4s²3d⁹
[Ar]4s²4d⁹
[Ar]4s²3p⁸
questions.explanation:
Copper (Cu) has atomic number 29.

 Its electron configuration is [Ar]4s¹3d¹⁰ instead of the expected [Ar]4s²3d⁹ because a fully filled d-orbital (3d¹⁰) is more stable than a fully filled s-orbital (4s²).

questions.questionText: What does Mendeleev's Periodic Law state? Properties of elements are periodic functions of their
options: atomic radius.
electron configurations.
atomic masses.
atomic numbers.
questions.explanation:
Mendeleev's Periodic Law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.

 Later, this law was refined by Moseley, who showed that properties are actually periodic with atomic numbers.

options: A.
B.
C.
D.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is correct regarding alkenes and alkynes?
options: The molecules of alkenes and alkynes are held together by weak intermolecular force.
Alkynes have longer bond length and larger face area than alkenes.
Alkenes are soluble in polar solvents, while alkynes are not soluble in polar solvents.
Alkenes and alkynes are soluble in polar solvents.
questions.explanation:
Alkenes and alkynes are nonpolar hydrocarbons.

 Their molecules interact mainly through weak van der Waals (dispersion) forces.

 They generally have low solubility in polar solvents and do not have longer bond lengths compared to alkanes or each other in the way described in option B.

questions.questionText: What is the general formula of alkynes?
options: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
CₙH₂ₙ
CₙHₙ₋₂ (n>2)
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (n≥2)
questions.explanation:
Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon–carbon triple bond. 

Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, where n is the number of carbon atoms and n ≥ 2.

questions.questionText: Which functional group containing compound is named using the suffix "-ol"?
options: Phenyl
Hydroxyl
Aryl
Carboxyl
questions.explanation:
Compounds containing the hydroxyl group (-OH) are named using the suffix '-ol'.

 These compounds are commonly known as alcohols.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the general formula of monohydric alcohols?
options: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH
CₙH₂ₙOH
CₙHₙ₋₂(OH)₂
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂OH
questions.explanation:
Monohydric alcohols contain only one hydroxyl (-OH) group.

 Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, where n is the number of carbon atoms.

questions.questionText: What is a Lewis acid? It is
options: a proton acceptor.
an electron pair donor.
an electron pair acceptor.
a proton donor.
questions.explanation: According to Lewis theory, a Lewis acid is a substance that can accept a pair of electrons to form a coordinate covalent bond, whereas a Lewis base donates an electron pair.

questions.questionText: What is enthalpy change? It is
options: the amount of heat absorbed in a reaction.
the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure and volume.
the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure.
the amount of heat given out in a reaction.
questions.explanation:
Enthalpy change (ΔH) is defined as the heat change that occurs during a chemical reaction carried out at constant pressure. 

It represents the difference in enthalpy between products and reactants.

questions.questionText: What is oxidation? Oxidation is
options: the reduction of the oxidation state of the oxidizing agent.
the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent.
the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.
the addition of hydrogen to a substance and the removal of oxygen from a substance.
questions.explanation:
Oxidation is defined as the process in which a species loses electrons, resulting in an increase in its oxidation number.

 This is a key concept in redox reactions.

questions.questionText: What is meant by preferential discharge, if a number of ions are present in a solution? It means that the one which requires
options: highest energy will be liberated last at a given electrode.
highest energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
least energy will be liberated last at a given electrode.
least energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
questions.explanation:
Preferential discharge refers to the tendency of ions in an electrolytic solution to be discharged at an electrode in the order of the energy required.

 The ion that requires the least energy for discharge will be discharged first.

questions.questionText: Faraday's Second Law states:
options: the amount of a substance consumed or produced at an electrode is inversely proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the solution.
the amount of a substance consumed or produced at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the solution.
passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their equivalent masses.
passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their molecular masses.
questions.explanation: Faraday's Second Law of Electrolysis states that when the same amount of electric charge passes through different electrolytes, the masses of substances deposited or liberated are proportional to their chemical equivalent weights (equivalent masses).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about Zn - Cu voltaic cell?
options: As the cell operates, electrons are continuously generated at the cathode and consumed at the anode.
The electrons flow from right to left through the external circuit.
After the cell runs for several hours, the Zn electrode weighs less.
The anode half-cell consists of a Cu electrode dipped into a Cu²⁺ solution.
questions.explanation:
In a Zn-Cu voltaic cell, zinc acts as the anode and undergoes oxidation, losing electrons and dissolving into Zn²⁺ ions.

 This causes the zinc electrode to decrease in mass over time. 

Electrons flow from the anode (Zn) to the cathode (Cu), and the Cu electrode gains mass as Cu²⁺ ions are reduced.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a polyprotic acid?
options: HNO₃
HF
H₃PO₄
HCl
questions.explanation:
A polyprotic acid is an acid that can donate more than one proton (H⁺) per molecule.

 H₃PO₄ (phosphoric acid) can donate three protons, making it a triprotic acid. 

The other acids listed (HNO₃, HF, HCl) are monoprotic, donating only one proton each.

questions.questionText: Which of the following does represent a general property of a base?
options: Aqueous solution of bases turns methyl orange to red.
Soluble bases release hydronium ion in aqueous solution.
Aqueous solution of bases turns blue litmus paper to red.
Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity.
questions.explanation:
Bases, especially strong bases, dissociate in water to produce hydroxide ions (OH⁻).

 This ionization allows the solution to conduct electricity. 

Other options are incorrect: bases turn red litmus blue, not the other way around; they do not release hydronium ions; and they turn methyl orange yellow, not red.

questions.questionText: What are salts? Salts are
options: ionic compounds formed by partial replacement of ionizable hydrogen by metal cations.
ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid.
ionic compounds that result from the reaction between metal hydroxide and water.
ionic compounds formed by complete replacement of ionizable hydrogen by anions of the acid.
questions.explanation:
Salts are ionic compounds formed when the hydrogen ion (H⁺) of an acid is replaced by a metal cation from a base. 

They consist of cations from a base and anions from an acid, and are usually formed during neutralization reactions.

questions.questionText: The process in which a compound absorbs electrical energy and decomposes into its elements is
options: electroplating.
hydrolysis.
solvolysis.
electrolysis.
questions.explanation:
Electrolysis is the process in which an electric current is passed through a compound (usually molten or in solution) causing it to decompose into its constituent elements.

 Examples include the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about galvanic cells used in commercial lead storage batteries?
options: The galvanic cells are made up of PbO₂ of anodes.
Half of the galvanic cells are connected in series.
Galvanic cells are connected to parallel.
Galvanic cells are connected in series.
questions.explanation:
In commercial lead-acid batteries, multiple galvanic cells are connected in series to increase the total voltage output.

 Each cell consists of a lead (Pb) anode and lead dioxide (PbO₂) cathode in sulfuric acid electrolyte.

questions.questionText: What is the mole ratio of oxygen gas to carbon dioxide gas in the following reaction? C₃H₈(g) + 50₂(g) ---> 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂0(l)
options: 7 mole oxygen gas to 5 mole carbon dioxide
2 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide
5 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide
10 mole oxygen gas to 6 mole carbon dioxide
questions.explanation:
From the balanced chemical equation, 1 mole of C₃H₈ reacts with 5 moles of O₂ to produce 3 moles of CO₂.

 Therefore, the mole ratio of O₂ to CO₂ is 5:3.

questions.questionText: Consider the following chemical equation for the combustion of ethane(C₂H₆)  in the presence of oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water: 2C₂H₆(g) + 7O₂ (g) -----> 4CO₂ (g) + 6H₂O (l). In this reaction:
options: CO₂ is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed.
water is formed at a rate equal to 2/3 the rate of formation of CO₂.
the rate of formation of CO₂ equals the rate of formation of water.
the rate of consumption of ethane is 7 times faster than the rate of consumption of oxygen.
questions.explanation:
From the balanced equation: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O

- Rate of formation of CO₂ / Rate of consumption of C₂H₆ = 4 / 2 = 2. So CO₂ is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed.

- Rate of formation of H₂O / Rate of formation of CO₂ = 6 / 4 = 3/2, not 2/3.

- Rates are proportional to stoichiometric coefficients.

- Rate of consumption of O₂ / Rate of consumption of C₂H₆ = 7 / 2, not 7 times faster.

Therefore, the correct statement is that CO₂ is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors DOES NOT affect the rate of a reaction?
options: Enthalpy
Temperature
Surface area
Concentration
questions.explanation:
The rate of a chemical reaction depends on factors like temperature, concentration of reactants, and surface area.

 Enthalpy (ΔH) affects the energy change of the reaction but does not directly influence the reaction rate.

questions.questionText: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
options: By changing the equilibrium constant
By lowering the activation energy
By increasing the activation energy
By forming an intermediate complex
questions.explanation:
A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

 It does not change the equilibrium constant but helps the reaction reach equilibrium faster.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle's Law?
options: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is directly proportional to the applied pressure.
questions.explanation:
Boyle's Law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, the volume of the gas is inversely proportional to its pressure (V ∝ 1/P).

 As pressure increases, volume decreases, and vice versa.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the formation of a covalent bond? In covalent bond electrons are
options: transferred from non-metallic atoms to metallic atoms.
shared between non-metallic atoms.
transferred from metallic atoms to non-metallic atoms.
shared between metallic atoms.
questions.explanation:
A covalent bond is formed when two non-metallic atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration.

 This sharing allows both atoms to attain noble gas configuration.

questions.questionText: How do the elements of Group IIA form ions?
options: By gaining 2 electrons
By losing 2 electrons
By losing one electron
By gaining one electron
questions.explanation:
Elements in Group IIA (alkaline earth metals) have two valence electrons in their outermost shell.

 They form ions by losing these two electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, resulting in a +2 charge.

questions.questionText: How is hydrogen bonding formed? It is formed when a hydrogen atom is bonded to
options: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
highly electronegative elements, chlorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
highly electronegative elements, fluorine oxygen and phosphorus.
highly electronegative elements, fluorine, chlorine and oxygen.
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen bonding occurs when a hydrogen atom is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen.

 The large difference in electronegativity creates a partial positive charge on hydrogen, which can then interact with lone pairs on nearby electronegative atoms, forming a hydrogen bond.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following forms of energy change occurs from the combustion of carbon in oxygen is
options: solar energy.
heat energy.
electrical energy.
light energy.
questions.explanation:
The combustion of carbon in oxygen (C + O₂ → CO₂) is an exothermic chemical reaction that releases energy in the form of heat. 

This heat energy can be used for heating, industrial processes, or generating electricity.

questions.questionText: What is the mole volume of a gas?
options: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 kPa ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 kPa ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 atm ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 atm ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
questions.explanation:
The molar volume of a gas is the volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP). 

By IUPAC definition, STP is 0°C (273.15 K) and 1 atm pressure.

 At these conditions, one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L.

questions.questionText: In the first order decomposition of dinitrogen pentoxide at 335 K N₂O₅ -----> 2NO₂ (g) + 1/2 O₂(g) . A reaction is carried out with 2.5 g N₂O₅ sample at 335 k and after 109 seconds, 1.50 g of N₂O₅  remained. What is the value of the rate constant?
questions.explanation:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant k can be calculated using the first-order integrated rate law:

ln([A]₀/[A]) = k * t

Given: [A]₀ = 2.5 g, [A] = 1.50 g, t = 109 s

k = ln(2.5 / 1.5) / 109

k = ln(1.6667) / 109 ≈ 0.5108 / 109 ≈ 4.69 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹

Therefore, the rate constant is 4.69 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between reversible and irreversible reactions?
options: In irreversible reactions, there is a mixture of products and reactants.
In reversible reactions, the reaction goes to completion.
In irreversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.
In reversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.
questions.explanation:
Reversible reactions can proceed in both forward and backward directions, eventually reaching a state of dynamic equilibrium where the rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal. 

Irreversible reactions proceed to completion, forming products without significant backward reaction.

questions.questionText: Consider the reactions all given bellow are in gaseous state. For which of the following reactions is Kₚ less than Kc?
options: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃
N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂
N₂ + O₂  ⇌ 2NO
2HI ⇌ H₂ + I₂
questions.explanation:
The relationship between Kₚ and Kc for a gaseous reaction is given by:

Kₚ = Kc(RT)^Δn

where Δn = moles of gaseous products - moles of gaseous reactants.

- A: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ → Δn = 2 - 3 = -1 → Kₚ < Kc ✅

- B: N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂ → Δn = 2 - 1 = +1 → Kₚ > Kc

- C: N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO → Δn = 2 - 2 = 0 → Kₚ = Kc

- D: 2HI ⇌ H₂ + I₂ → Δn = 2 - 2 = 0 → Kₚ = Kc

Therefore, Kₚ is less than Kc only for reaction A.

questions.questionText: The general formula for saturated monocarboxylic acids is
options: RCOOH
RCOOH
ROR
RCHO
questions.explanation:
Saturated monocarboxylic acids contain one carboxyl functional group (–COOH) and no double or triple bonds in the hydrocarbon chain. 

Their general representation is RCOOH, where R is a saturated alkyl group.

 Options C (ROR) represents ethers, and D (RCHO) represents aldehydes, so they are incorrect.

questions.questionText: What is the concentration of a solution? It is
options: number of moles of solute and number of moles of solvent.
the amount of solute needed to make a concentrated solute.
the amount of solvent needed to dissolve a solute.
the quantity of solute in a given quantity of solution.
questions.explanation:
The concentration of a solution describes how much solute is present in a given amount of solution. 

Option D is correct because it directly states that concentration is the quantity of solute in a given quantity of solution.

 The other options either describe moles separately or focus only on solute or solvent, which does not define concentration.

questions.questionText: How many moles of C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ (sucrose, Molecular weight 342.91 g/mol) is needed there to prepare 2.0L of 0.3M solution?
questions.explanation:
Molarity (M) is defined as moles of solute per liter of solution. 

Using the formula M = n / V, where n is number of moles and V is volume in liters: n = M × V = 0.3 mol/L × 2.0 L = 0.6 mol. 

Therefore, 0.6 moles of sucrose are needed.

questions.questionText: At 75 °C, the vapor pressure of pure water is 39 kPa. Which one of the vapor pressure of a solution obtained by dissolving 34.2 g sucrose in 180 mL of water? (Assume that the density of water is 1.000 g/mL)
options: 44.5kPa
41.1 kPa
38.6 kPa
31.2 kPa
questions.explanation:
We can calculate the vapor pressure of the solution using Raoult's Law:

Pₐ = Xₐ * Pₐ⁰ Where:n- Pₐ⁰ = vapor pressure of pure solvent = 39 kPa

- Xₐ = mole fraction of solvent

Step 1: Calculate moles of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁, M = 342 g/mol):

 n_sucrose = 34.2 / 342 ≈ 0.1 mol

Step 2: Calculate moles of water (H₂O, M = 18 g/mol):

 Mass of water = 180 mL × 1 g/mL = 180 g

 n_water = 180 / 18 = 10 mol

Step 3: Mole fraction of water:

 X_water = n_water / (n_water + n_sucrose) = 10 / (10 + 0.1) ≈ 0.9901

Step 4: Vapor pressure of solution:

 P_solution = X_water * Pₐ⁰ ≈ 0.9901 × 39 ≈ 38.6 kPa

So the vapor pressure of the solution is approximately 38.6 kPa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE about the colligative properties of electrolytes and non-electrolytes?
options: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is the same as those of electrolytes.
The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is very low compared to electrolytes.
The colligative properties of non-electrolytes are not considerably changed.
The effect of electrolytes on colligative properties is very high compared to non-electrolytes.
questions.explanation:
Colligative properties depend on the number of particles in solution.

 Electrolytes dissociate into ions, producing more particles, so they have a much greater effect on colligative properties than non-electrolytes. 

Therefore, it is NOT TRUE that non-electrolytes have the same effect as electrolytes.

 Options B, C, and D correctly describe the weaker effect of non-electrolytes and the stronger effect of electrolytes.

questions.questionText:
For the reaction shown below, which of the following is a conjugate acid-base pair? 

 HC₂O₄⁻(aq) + H₂O ⇌ H₃O + C₂0₄²⁻
options: HC₂O₄⁻ and C₂O₄²⁻
H₃O⁺ and HC₂O₄⁻
H₂O and C₂O₄²⁻
HC₂O₄⁻ and H₂O
questions.explanation:
A conjugate acid-base pair consists of two species that differ by a single proton (H⁺). In the reaction:

HC₂O₄⁻ + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + C₂O₄²⁻

- HC₂O₄⁻ donates a proton to form C₂O₄²⁻ → they are a conjugate acid-base pair.

- H₂O accepts a proton to form H₃O⁺ → they are also a conjugate acid-base pair.

Among the options, HC₂O₄⁻ and C₂O₄²⁻ correctly represent one conjugate acid-base pair.

questions.questionText: Which of the following assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the high compressibility of gases?
options: Different particles have different speeds.
Particles are always in random motion.
There is no force of attraction between gas molecules.
The actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.
questions.explanation:
According to the kinetic molecular theory, gas molecules occupy negligible volume compared to the total volume of the container.

 This means there is a lot of empty space between gas particles, allowing the gas to be easily compressed. 

Therefore, the assumption that explains the high compressibility of gases is that the actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.

questions.questionText: Consider a bottle containing water, water vapor and air in equilibrium. If the temperature decreases slightly, the amount of water vapor:
options: and vapor pressure will decrease.
will decrease and the vapor pressure will increase.
will increase and the vapor pressure will decrease.
and vapor pressure will increase.
questions.explanation:
In a closed container at equilibrium, the vapor pressure of water depends only on temperature.

 When the temperature decreases, the equilibrium vapor pressure decreases.

 As a result, some water vapor condenses into liquid water, so the amount of water vapor also decreases.

questions.questionText: Why do water droplets collect on the outside of a glass of water on a hot day?
options: There will be a sublimation of water vapor on the outside of a glass.
There will be a condensation of water vapor on the glass.
Water from the glass starts to vaporize.
There is heat exchange between the water in the glass and the surrounding.
questions.explanation:
On a hot day, the air contains water vapor.

 When this warm, moist air comes into contact with the cooler surface of the glass, the water vapor loses energy and changes into liquid droplets. 

This process is called condensation.

questions.questionText: What are hydrocarbons? Compounds that contain
options: benzene and its derivatives only.
benzene rings only.
hydrogen and carbon only.
hydrogen and carbon with no benzene rings.
questions.explanation:
Hydrocarbons are organic compounds composed exclusively of hydrogen and carbon atoms.

 They can be alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, or aromatic compounds (like benzene), but the defining feature is that they contain only hydrogen and carbon.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT regarding the boiling points of alkanes?
options: The boiling point of cycloalkanes is higher than that of linear alkanes.
Boiling points of straight chain alkanes is greater than that of branched chain alkanes.
Surface area is the only factor that determines the boiling points of alkanes.
Boiling points increases with stronger Van der Waals forces.
questions.explanation:
The boiling point of alkanes depends on molecular size, surface area, and intermolecular forces (Van der Waals forces).

 While linear alkanes generally have higher boiling points than branched ones due to greater surface area, it is incorrect to say that surface area is the only factor.

 Cycloalkanes, branching, and molecular weight also affect boiling points.

questions.questionText: The self-ionization of water can be expressed by the equation: H₂O(l) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺ (aq) + OH⁻(aq) Which of the following is the correct expression of the ionic product of water?
options: Kw = [H₃O⁺,OH]/[H₂O]
Kw = [H₃O⁺,OH⁻]
Kw = Kc(H₂O)
Kw = Kc(H₂O)²
questions.explanation:
In the self-ionization of water:

H₂O(l) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)

The ionic product of water, Kw, is defined as the product of the concentrations of H₃O⁺ and OH⁻ in aqueous solution. Since the concentration of liquid water is effectively constant, it is included in the equilibrium constant to give Kw:

Kw = [H₃O⁺,OH⁻]

questions.questionText: What is the effect of a common ion in an electrolytic solution?
options: It has no effect on the pH of a solution.
It decreases the solubility of a solute.
It suppresses the imitation of a weak base and lowers the pOH.
It suppresses the imitation of a weak acid and raises the pH.
questions.explanation:
The common ion effect occurs when a solution already contains an ion that is part of a dissolved salt or weak acid/base equilibrium.

 This extra ion shifts the equilibrium according to Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing the solubility of the solute and suppressing ionization.

 Therefore, the main effect is a decrease in solubility of the solute.

questions.questionText: Sodium carbonate is a basic salt because it is a salt of
options: a strong acid and a weak base and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed.
a weak acid and a weak base and the cation of the weak base can be hydrolyzed.
a strong base and a strong acid and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed.
a strong base and a weak acid and the anion of the weak acid can be hydrolyzed.
questions.explanation:
Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is a salt formed from a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (H₂CO₃).

 In water, the carbonate ion (CO₃²⁻) can hydrolyze, producing OH⁻ ions, which makes the solution basic. 

Therefore, it is a basic salt because it comes from a strong base and a weak acid, and the anion of the weak acid undergoes hydrolysis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for an acid-base titration?
options: An acid-base titration is a method of qualitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base.
An acid-base titration is a method of quantitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base.
Acid-base titrations cannot be carried out in the absence of indicators.
Indicators catalyze an acid-base titration to show the inflection point of the titration curve.
questions.explanation:
An acid-base titration is a quantitative analytical method used to determine the unknown concentration of an acid or base by reacting it with a base or acid of known concentration.

 Indicators are used to show the end point, but they do not catalyze the reaction, and titrations can theoretically be monitored by other means (e.g., pH meters).

 Therefore, the correct statement is that it is a method of quantitative analysis.

questions.questionText: What is the change in internal energy (ΔE) for a reaction, in which the system absorbs 650 J of heat and 125 J of work is done on the system?
questions.explanation:
The change in internal energy is given by the first law of thermodynamics:

ΔE = q + w

Where:- q = heat absorbed by the system (positive if absorbed) = +650 J

- w = work done on the system (positive if done on the system) = +125 J

So, ΔE = 650 + 125 = 775 J

Therefore, the change in internal energy is +775 J.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is correct regarding alkenes and alkynes?
options: The molecules of alkenes and alkynes are held together by weak intermolecular forces.
Alkynes have longer bond length and less surface area than alkenes.
Alkenes are soluble in polar solvents, while alkynes are not soluble in polar solvents.
Alkenes and alkynes are soluble in polar solvents.
questions.explanation:
Alkenes and alkynes are nonpolar hydrocarbons, so they are held together by weak Van der Waals (dispersion) forces.

 They are generally insoluble in polar solvents like water but soluble in nonpolar solvents.

 Alkynes have shorter bond lengths (triple bond) than alkenes (double bond).

 Therefore, the correct statement is that their molecules are held together by weak intermolecular forces.

questions.questionText: What is the general formula of alkynes?
options: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
CₙH₂ₙ
CₙHₙ₋₂ (n>2)
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (n≥2)
questions.explanation:
Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon–carbon triple bond. 

Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, where n is the number of carbon atoms and n ≥ 2.

questions.questionText: Which functional group containing compound is named using the suffix "-ol"?
options: Phenyl
Hydroxyl
Aryl
Carboxyl
questions.explanation:
Compounds containing the hydroxyl group (-OH) are named using the suffix '-ol'.

 These compounds are commonly known as alcohols.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the general formula of monohydric alcohols?
options: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH
CₙH₂ₙOH
CₙHₙ₋₂(OH)₂
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂OH
questions.explanation:
Monohydric alcohols contain only one hydroxyl (-OH) group.

 Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, where n is the number of carbon atoms.

questions.questionText: What is a Lewis acid? It is
options: a proton acceptor.
an electron pair donor.
an electron pair acceptor.
a proton donor.
questions.explanation: According to Lewis theory, a Lewis acid is a substance that can accept a pair of electrons to form a coordinate covalent bond, whereas a Lewis base donates an electron pair.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT CORRECT about minerals and ores?
options: Ores are usually used to extract metals economically.
Minerals are the natural forms in which various metals exist.
All ores are minerals.
All minerals are ores.
questions.explanation:
Minerals are naturally occurring substances that contain metals or other elements. 

Ores are minerals or rocks from which metals can be extracted economically.

 Not all minerals are ores, because some minerals contain metals in very low concentrations that are not economically feasible to extract.

 Therefore, the statement that all minerals are ores is NOT correct.

questions.questionText: Why is CaCl₂ added to NaCl in a 1:1 1/2 ratio in the Down's cell for the manufacturing of sodium metal?
options: CaCl₂ is used as an electrolyte.
CaCl₂ is used to lower the density of the mixture.
CaCl₂ is used to lower the melting temperature of NaCl.
CaCl₂ is used as a catalyst.
questions.explanation:
In the Down's cell for sodium production, pure NaCl has a very high melting point (about 801 °C). 

Adding CaCl₂ lowers the melting point of the mixture, allowing electrolysis to occur at a lower temperature, which reduces energy consumption and prevents sodium from reacting with the container.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a major step in metallurgical processes?
options: Extracting the metal and refining
Pretreatment
Concentrating the ore
Mining the ore
questions.explanation:
The major steps in metallurgical processes typically include: (1) Concentrating the ore, (2) Extracting the metal, and (3) Refining the metal.

 Pretreatment is sometimes included depending on context, but 'Mining the ore' is not considered a metallurgical process step—it is part of mining engineering, not metallurgy.

questions.questionText: Which monomers are used for the synthesis of Teflon?
options: Tetrafluoroethylene
Styrene and Phenol
Propylene
Isoprene
questions.explanation:
Teflon, also known as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), is synthesized by the polymerization of tetrafluoroethylene monomers.

 Other options like styrene, phenol, propylene, and isoprene are used to make different polymers such as polystyrene, phenolic resins, polypropylene, and synthetic rubber, respectively.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the structure of a disaccharide?
options: A.
B.
C.
D.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of synthetic cryolite in the extraction of aluminum by the Hall's process?
options: Cryolite is used as a catalyst in the extraction of aluminum.
Cryolite increases the melting point of alumina.
Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.
Cryolite increases the purity of the extracted aluminum.
questions.explanation:
In the Hall-Héroult process for extracting aluminum, alumina (Al₂O₃) has a very high melting point (~2072°C).

 Synthetic cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to dissolve alumina and reduce its melting point to about 900°C, making electrolysis practical and energy-efficient.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a chemical property of aluminum?
options: Aluminum has a lower density than any other commercial metal.
Aluminum is a good conductor of heat and electricity.
Aluminum is a grey metal in color.
Aluminum liberates hydrogen gas from dilute acids like HCl and H₂SO₄.
questions.explanation:
Chemical properties describe how a substance reacts with other substances. 

Aluminum reacts with dilute acids such as HCl or H₂SO₄ to liberate hydrogen gas, which is a chemical reaction.

 The other options (A, B, C) describe physical properties, not chemical properties.

questions.questionText: How is tanning carried out? In tanning the hides or skins are
options: treated with dilute hydrochloric acid to remove the lime.
treated with chromium salts.
soaked in lime and water for several days.
soaked in water for several days.
questions.explanation:
Tanning is the process of converting raw hides or skins into leather, making them durable and less prone to decomposition. 

This is typically done by treating the hides with chromium salts (like chromium(III) sulfate), which cross-link the collagen fibers in the skin.

questions.questionText: How can a project of establishing an industry that consumes coal affect the environment?
options: By changing the pH of water
Production of high level of lead in the atmosphere
Rise in global temperature
Increment in concentration of nitric oxide
questions.explanation:
Industries that consume coal release large amounts of carbon dioxide (CO₂) and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

 This contributes to the greenhouse effect, leading to a rise in global temperature, commonly referred to as global warming.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity SI unit?
options: Length
Pressure
Force
Speed
questions.explanation:
In the SI system, fundamental (base) quantities are those that are not derived from other quantities.

 Length is a fundamental quantity measured in meters (m). 

Pressure, force, and speed are derived quantities calculated from base quantities.

questions.questionText: What are intermolecular forces? They are forces due to the attraction between
options: cations and delocalized electrons.
nuclei and electron pair.
cations and anions.
molecules.
questions.explanation:
Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction or repulsion that act between neighboring molecules.

 These forces include Van der Waals forces (dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions) and hydrogen bonding, all of which occur between molecules.

questions.questionText: Which of the following belongs to chemical bonding theories?
options: Valence bond theory and Valence shell electron pair repulsion theory.
Molecular orbital theory and kinetic-molecular theory.
Valence bond theory and molecular orbital theory.
Kinetic-molecular theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory.
questions.explanation: Chemical bonding theories explain how atoms combine to form molecules. Valence Bond (VB) theory and Molecular Orbital (MO) theory are both fundamental theories describing chemical bonding. Other options like VSEPR theory describe molecular shapes, and kinetic-molecular theory describes gas behavior, not bonding.

questions.questionText: In which of the following molecules is the central atom SP² hybridized?
options: CO
SO₂
N₂O
CO₂
questions.explanation:
SP² hybridization occurs when a central atom forms three regions of electron density (bonds or lone pairs). 

In SO₂, the sulfur atom forms two double bonds with oxygen and has one lone pair, giving three regions of electron density, which corresponds to SP² hybridization.

 In contrast, CO and N₂O have linear structures with SP hybridization, and CO₂ is linear with SP hybridization as well.

questions.questionText: For a reaction: 1/2 A --------->  2B the rate of disappearance of 'A' is related to the appearance of 'B' by the expression:
options: -Δ[A]/Δt = 1/4* Δ[B]/Δt
-Δ[A]/Δt = 1/2* Δ[B]/Δt
-Δ[A]/Δt  = 4Δ[B]/Δt
Δ[A]/Δt = Δ[B]/Δt
questions.explanation:
The rate of a reaction is related to the change in concentration of reactants and products, taking into account stoichiometric coefficients:

Rate = - (1/ν_A) Δ[A]/Δt = (1/ν_B) Δ[B]/Δt

Here, the reaction is (1/2)A → 2B, so ν_A = 1/2 and ν_B = 2.

Rate = - (1 / (1/2)) Δ[A]/Δt = (1 / 2) Δ[B]/Δt

Rate = -2 Δ[A]/Δt = 1/2 Δ[B]/Δt

Rewriting gives: -Δ[A]/Δt = 1/4 Δ[B]/Δt

questions.questionText: The half-life of a reaction is the time taken for the
options: complete conversion of a reactant into a product.
rate constant to decrease by 50% of its initial value.
rate constant to increase by 50% of its initial value.
reactant concentration to decrease by 50% of its initial value.
questions.explanation:
The half-life of a reaction is defined as the time required for the concentration of a reactant to decrease to half of its initial value.

 It is independent of the rate constant changing; rather, it is directly related to the decay of the reactant.

questions.questionText: For the conversion of 3.5 yards into meter using the factor label method, which of the following is the correct step?
options: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(1 foot/ 112 in )(2.54 cm/1 in)(1m/100cm)
(3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/ 1 foot )(1 in/2.54 cm/)(1m/100cm)
(3.5 yards/1)(1 yard/3.5 feet)(12 in/ 1 foot )(2.54 cm/1 in)(1m/100cm)
(3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/ 1 foot )(2.54 cm/1 in)(1m/100cm)
questions.explanation:
To convert 3.5 yards to meters using the factor-label (unit conversion) method, we follow the correct sequence of conversion factors:

1 yard = 3 feet → multiply by 3 feet / 1 yard

1 foot = 12 inches → multiply by 12 in / 1 foot

1 inch = 2.54 cm → multiply by 2.54 cm / 1 in

100 cm = 1 m → multiply by 1 m / 100 cm

So the correct setup is:

(3.5 yards / 1) × (3 feet / 1 yard) × (12 in / 1 foot) × (2.54 cm / 1 in) × (1 m / 100 cm).

questions.questionText: In the scientific method, a predictive statement that can be tested experimentally is:
options: hypothesis.
proof.
evidence.
truth.
questions.explanation:
In the scientific method, a hypothesis is a predictive statement or proposed explanation that can be tested through experiments and observations.

 Proof, evidence, and truth are results or conclusions, not the initial testable statement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about cathode rays? Cathode rays
options: are common constituents of all matter and their m/e is constant for all gases.
contain particles, which are positively charged.
travel in straight lines from cathode to the anode.
contain particles, which are negatively charged.
questions.explanation:
Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which are negatively charged particles.

 They travel in straight lines in vacuum and have the same charge-to-mass ratio (e/m) for all gases.

 They are not positively charged, so the statement that they contain positively charged particles is NOT true.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is correct about the energy of a photon?
options: It is directly proportional to the wave length of the light.
It is directly related to the intensity of the light.
It is inversely proportional to the observed frequency of the light.
It is directly proportional to the observed frequency of the light.
questions.explanation:
The energy of a photon is given by the equation E = hν, where h is Planck's constant and ν is the frequency of the light.

 Therefore, the energy is directly proportional to the frequency of the light. 
It is not proportional to wavelength or intensity, and it is not inversely proportional to frequency.

questions.questionText: Which of the following explains the emission spectra of atoms consisting of a series of fine lines?
options: An electron that revolves around the nucleus emits radiation.
The energy of the atoms is continuous with discreet frequencies.
An electron undergoes a transition by energy changes corresponding to photon of specific wave length.
An electron can have specific energy values in an atom.
questions.explanation: The emission spectra of atoms appear as a series of fine lines because electrons occupy discrete energy levels in an atom. When an electron transitions from a higher energy level to a lower one, it emits a photon with a specific wavelength corresponding to the energy difference. This explains the line spectra observed.
